name: Water Deluge Sound Suppression System
summary: High-flow gravity-fed water tower and trench manifold that floods the launch mount with water seconds before Merlin 1D ignition.
function: Absorbs extreme acoustic energy and thermal flux from 9× Merlin 1D engines (7.6 MN) to protect the vehicle and payload from reflected sound waves.
materials: Elevated steel water storage tank, high-capacity butterfly deluge valves, and reinforced steel spray nozzles ringing the launch mount and flame trench.

specs.label: LC-39A Tank Capacity
specs.source: NASA KSC LC-39A Sound Suppression Water System (~300,000 gal)

specs.label: LC-39A Tower Height
specs.source: NASA KSC LC-39A elevated water tower (~290 ft)

specs.label: Deluge Activation
specs.source: Representative pre-ignition deluge start (varies by site/mission)

history: Originally installed for Space Shuttle launches to prevent overpressure waves from damaging the orbiter, the deluge system flashes thousands of liters of water per second into billowing ground-hugging steam at Falcon 9 ignition.
sources: NASA KSC Sound Suppression Water System Reference
